News.title: Dramatic moment hero school principal tackles gunman, 20, to the ground just as he opens fire and ‘saves kids’ lives’
News.content:
THIS is the jaw-dropping moment a school principal boldly tackles a school shooter as he prepares to open fire on students.

Breathtaking CCTV footage shows the hooded gunman enter the school lobby, brandishing a pistol in hand.





A man suddenly appears, tackling the shooter onto a nearby bench.

With his hand firmly clasped around the suspect‘s wrist, the heroic individual desperately calls for help.

Another member of staff quickly arrives as the suspect finally lets go of the weapon.

In the aftermath of the harrowing ordeal, it was revealed the selfless act was carried out by the school’s principal Kirk Moore.

During the confrontation with the suspect, Moore sustained a bullet wound to the leg and was subsequently hospitalised.

Moore has since expressed his gratitude for the “outpouring of love and support” following the incident at Pauls Valley High School last Tuesday.

The principal added that he is “healthy and recovering” and looks forward to returning to work as soon as he is able to do so.



In an arrest affidavit, investigators said Victor Lee Hawkins walked into the lobby of the school armed with two automatic handguns.

The 20-year-old told everyone to get on the ground before trying to shoot one student, only to be thwarted by a malfunctioning weapon.

After clearing the blockage, Hawkins opened fire on another student but missed.

The two students then pleaded for mercy and were allowed to leave just as Moore tackled Hawkins from behind.

A former pupil at the school, Hawkins, described Moore as someone he “did not like”, according to prosecutors.



He allegedly said he “wanted to conduct his own school shooting like the Columbine shooters did” – referring to a deadly Colorado high school massacre back in 1999.

Investigators say Hawkins admitted to going to school equipped with two firearms belonging to his father.

They further allege that he took them without his parent’s permission.

The affidavit then claims his intention was to kill both students and faculty members.

Once this was completed, he planned to kill Moore and then turn the gun on himself, the affidavit said.



Pauls Valley Police Chief Don May said Moore’s selfless act likely thwarted a tragedy.

“It doesn’t surprise me the actions that he took, but it is amazing, the actions that he took,” he said.

“There’s no doubt in my mind that he saved kids’ lives.”

Hawkins has since been taken into custody at the Garvin County Detention Center with a $1 million bail bond.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

According to court documents, he has been charged with shooting with intent to kill, feloniously pointing a firearm and carrying a weapon to a public assembly.



Hawkins is now scheduled to appear in court on May 8 for a preliminary hearing.

News.title: Second school shooting in just 24hrs ‘leaves four dead and six injured’ in Turkey
News.content:
AT least four people have died in a second Turkish school shooting in just 24 hours.

An armed attacker – understood to be a 16-year-old former student – has reportedly killed three students and a teacher in a horror rampage on Wednesday.





The governor of Türkiye’s southern province of Kahramanmaraş confirmed there was an ongoing attack.

“A tragic incident occurred in one of our schools,” Mükerrem Ünlüer said.

The governor later issued a separate statement aired live, confirming fatalities at Ayser Calik Secondary School.

He said three students and a teacher were killed and several others were wounded.

Earlier reports feared there may be up to 20 people dead.

It comes 24 hours after a former student armed with a pump-action shotgun began firing randomly at a different school yesterday.

At least 16 people were injured in that attack at the high school in the country’s south east.

Distressing CCTV footage shows the shooter charge towards the school doors as some of his panicked classmates recognise the danger and begin to flee.



The teen then enters the building and looks down at his rifle before beginning his rampage.

Terrified students can be seen running for their lives and barricading themselves in classrooms as the gunman makes his way down the hall.

The full video of the incident is too distressing to show in its entirety.

The attack has left 10 students, four teachers, a canteen employee and a police officer wounded, authorities said.

Governor Hasan Sildak told local media that the 19-year-old shooter took his own life when cops cornered him.



He added: “We have evacuated the school and will carry out a thorough investigation into this tragic incident.”

Cops rushed to Siverek, in the country’s southeast, on Tuesday morning after locals reported gunshots coming from the high school.

Early reports indicated the attacker may have taken some students hostage.

A witness told local media he saw “a kid” pull out a long-barrelled gun.

The attacker first opened fire in the yard before directing the gun towards the school, the witness said.



He added: “He fired at everyone in his path inside.”

It’s understood the assailant then hid inside the building.

Police special operations units were deployed to Ahmet Koyuncu Vocational and Technical Anatolian High School after the assailant refused to surrender.

All staff and students were evacuated and the school and surrounding area were cordoned off by security forces.

News.title: Europe’s secret plan for a NEW Nato without US gains traction after Trump’s threats leave door open for Putin to invade
News.content:
EUROPEAN nations are hatching a secret plan to form a new Nato – as the looming threat of US withdrawal makes the continent vulnerable to Vladimir Putin.

Anxiety within the alliance has reached a fever pitch over the past few weeks, with Donald Trump repeatedly threatening to withdraw over its inaction in the Iran war.





The plan for a new partnership, which was informally conceived last year, is not intended to rival the current alliance, but to provide a stronger buffer against Russian invasion in the face of American unreliability.

Officials working on the “European Nato” plan are reportedly trying to supplement US military assets with European ones.



Trump’s threat to seize Greenland from Denmark is said to have moved the plan up the priority list and it has since gained even more urgency in the wake of the Iran war.

It has been boosted after a spectacular reversal from Germany, which has long defended America’s position as the ultimate guarantor of European security.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz has changed the tide by deciding to engage with scheme, giving the proposal some much-needed wind.

But the challenge to build a new pact from scratch will be enormous.



Nato’s structure is built around American leadership at nearly every level, from the alliance’s top military command to logistics.

The US has the majority of the pact‘s nuclear weapons, tanks, aircraft and troops meaning if Trump was serious about leaving for good then the battle to replace America’s military might would be nigh-on impossible.

Trump is reportedly weighing up punishing “unhelpful” Nato nations by withdrawing troops from their bases and redeploying them to countries who have been supportive of Washington.

Nato chief Mark Rutte said he understands Washington‘s frustrations as he even agreed with Trump, saying: “Not all European nations lived up to those commitments [in Iran].”

The US president aimed a fresh barb at Nato earlier today, writing that “it wasn’t there for us [in Iran], and they won’t be there for us in the future!”



By law, the Trump administration wouldn’t be able to remove the US from Nato without Congressional approval first.

Trump has repeatedly blasted America’s allies for failing to come to its aid in the Iran war, and claimed that – like Russian tyrant Vladimir Putin – he knows that Nato is a “paper tiger”.

He branded the alliance as “terrible”, telling fuel-starved members “get your own oil” after they failed to send warships and help release the Strait of Hormuz from Iran’s grip.

Asked by the Telegraph if he would reconsider the alliance, Trump said: “Oh yes, I would say [it’s] beyond reconsideration.



“I was never swayed by Nato. I always knew they were a paper tiger, and Putin knows that too, by the way.”

Ex-British intelligence officer and former Nato planner Philip Ingram warns that the idea of Nato without the US is “very significant” to Europe‘s security.

He told The Sun that during his years as a top coordinator for the alliance he was actively involved in plans which touched on Nato without US support.

He believes that Nato nations would be confident in their ability to remain as a strong global force but that they would scramble to act quickly to convince any lurking enemies.



Ingram said: “Getting a public message that shows Nato unity, if the United States decides to pull out, would be critical.

“And that message of unity would need to send a clear message to particularly Vladimir Putin.

“But then turning that message of unity and the words into actual practical change is always the hardest part.”

Britain’s Sir Keir Starmer staunchly defended Nato as “the single most effective military alliance the world has ever seen”.



But the UK leader has been on the receiving end of much of Trump’s ire across the war.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Trump has threatened to rip up his trade deal with Britain over Starmer’s lack of support.

The US President said his tariff arrangement with the UK was “better than I had to” and “can always be changed” in the wake of souring relations.

News.title: Prison officer who smuggled £35k of drugs into jail for lag lover flaunts freedom on TikTok with string of boasting vids
News.content:
A BRAZEN former prison officer who tried to smuggle £35,000 of drugs into jail for her lag lover has been flaunting her freedom on TikTok.

Olivia Johnson, 28, was put behind bars for three-and-a-half years in July last year after she was caught trying to smuggle spice into HMP Highpoint for her inmate lover.





Johnson served just a year of her sentence after being caught with the synthetic drug and has now turned to TikTok to show off her post-prison life.

Following her release from Askham Grange women’s prison in York earlier this month, Johnson immediately began to make videos for her 43,000 followers.

The shamed inmate-turned-influencer now shares footage of her DIY projects on TikTok and talks openly about her crimes.



Johnson’s clips involve her cats, food, and footage of her doing up her new-build home in South Yorkshire.

She told fans how she was nervous to explain that she had been in prison but now the ex-guard regularly talks about her sentence.

Johnson answers questions from her followers about her time in jail; in one video, she tells her tens of thousands of fans how she managed her mortgage while behind bars.

In the footage, the ex-prison officer, who worked briefly as an estate agent, thanked her family and friends for supporting her with her bills while she was locked up.



Johnson said: “I’ll forever be grateful to the support I’ve had from my family/friends.

“I made very stupid choices which have impacted them and I will spend the rest of my life making it up to them.”

In another clip shared on the shamed prison officer’s TikTok, she appears to share footage of the moment she was granted her freedom.

Footage shows her walking out of the front gates of the prison where she was held, carrying several bags.

She rushes to meet an unidentified man waiting for her outside the prison walls before leaping into his arms.



The pair share an embrace and a kiss before laughing as the clip comes to an end.

Johnson captioned the video of her release: “Let me explain… ready for my soft girl era.”



The shamed prison officer said she: “Never felt so anxious posting a video in my life, but I decided that I just had to rip the bandage off and let everybody know where I’ve been because I cannot hide the fact and I’m not gonna let it define me.”

Johnson worked at HMP Highpoint for three years before being stopped in a random check as she arrived for work in September 2022.

After searching her, Johnson’s former colleagues discovered 88 sheets of paper that had been soaked in the synthetic drug spice.

A court was later told that she had tried to smuggle the drugs into the prison for London gang member Javelle Taylor, who was serving a 12-year sentence for firearms offences.

Detectives later found messages between the shamed prison officer and the crook after a phone was recovered from Johnson’s red Toyota Aygo.



Message exchanges found on the phone revealed the pair had been having an “intimate relationship,” with Johnson declaring her love for the lag in a slew of flirty texts.

Investigators also discovered that associates of Taylor had paid some £15,000 into Johnson’s bank account over a nine-month period.

It was said in court that Johnson had become “emotionally dependent” on the jailed gangster.

During her sentencing, her defence barrister explained she was remorseful and had become trapped in the relationship with Taylor.

But, sentencing her last July, Recorder Richard Christie KC described her crimes as “serious”.



The judge said her actions “strike at the heart of the integrity of the criminal justice system”.

He added: “In the pre-sentence report, the author records that although you say you committed these offences because you were in an intimate relationship with the prisoner, Javelle Taylor, that it is more likely that they were committed for financial gain.

“I take the view that it’s a bit of both. Both financial gain and because you professed love for him.”

Johnson admitted misconduct in a public office, acquiring criminal property and conspiring to take contraband into prison.

Now, having served less than half of her three-year sentence, Johnson is brazenly portraying herself online as a changed woman.



Speaking to her legion of followers, Johnson explained that her time behind bars had been “tough”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In one exchange online with a follower, she said, “I deserved my time, and it’s given me time to reflect and grow!

“Ready to start fresh with it all behind me.”

News.title: Boy, 16, stabbed to death outside shopping centre is pictured as family pay heartbreaking tribute
News.content:
'NEVER FORGOTTEN' Boy, 16, stabbed to death outside shopping centre is pictured as family pay heartbreaking tribute

A TEENAGER who was fatally stabbed outside a busy shopping centre has been pictured for the first time – as his devastated family pay tribute.

Four teens were arrested after Baye Bireme Fall, 16, was attacked near the Orton Centre in Peterborough, Cambridgeshire, on Sunday evening.





Cops were scrambled to a report that a teen had been attacked outside the busy shopping centre at around 7pm.

Baye was rushed to hospital by paramedics but, despite the best efforts of medical teams, the teen sadly died a short while later.

In a touching tribute released through cops, his heartbroken family hailed him as an “amazing boy and son”.

They said: “We are completely shattered and may never recover from the passing away of our son whose life was tragically cut short.

“Baye was an amazing boy and son whose heart is pure and kind towards other people.

“He was ever so ready to lend a helping hand to anyone who was in need. His kindness and generosity will never be forgotten.”

Investigators from Cambridgeshire Police quickly launched a murder probe into the tragedy.

The force later arrested a 15-year-old boy and an 18-year-old man on suspicion of murder.



They remain in custody as detectives continue to appeal for information.

Two girls, aged 17 and 16, were also arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender.

The force has urged anyone with information to report it online or by calling 101, quoting Op Whitby.

DCI Richard Stott, from the Beds, Cambs and Herts Major Crime Unit, confirmed the family were being supported by specialist officers.

He added: “This is a tragic incident which has resulted in the death of a young man.



“While we understand the death will be concerning for local people, we do not believe this was a random attack.

“There will be a significant police presence in the area over coming days.

“I would urge anyone who believes they have information about this attack, or lives in the area and has CCTV at their home, to contact police.”

News.title: Over 85,000 households to be visited in UK over recalled tumble dryer that poses ‘serious risk of fire’
News.content:
A SAFETY alert warning has been issued to thousands of UK homes over tumble dryers that could catch fire after use.

In December last year, the government confirmed that safety regulators had identified a string of tumble dryers, made by well-known brands, could pose a major fire risk.



The issue is caused by an integrated heat-pump inside the tumble dryers, which could burst into flames due to an electrical fault during normal use.



As a result, households were told not to use the impacted dryers under any circumstances.

The dryers impacted were manufactured by Baumatic, Candy, Caple, Haier, Hoover, Lamona, Iberna and Montpellier.

However, owners are encouraged to check their model and serial numbers to see if their dryer is affected or not.

The appliance must not be used until the repair has been completed. If the plug is accessible, owners have been advised to switch it off and unplug the dryer.

Yesterday the Office for Product Safety and Standards (OPPS) gave an update saying companies would be visiting homes affected by the recall.

In a product safety alert, it was stated that the manufacturing companies will visit every home containing affected tumble dryers and make them safe.

The OPSS stated: “The UK manufacturers have initiated a modification programme for products in scope of the safety issue. The companies will visit every home containing affected tumble dryers and make them safe.



“OPSS is urging all affected members of the public, including those unsure whether they are impacted or not, to check the model links and contact the manufacturer.”

They can also consult the official GOV.UK product safety alert website or check the safety pages on the websites of Baumatic, Candy, Caple, Haier, Hoover, Iberna, Lamona and Montpellier.

This next step comes after the OPPS initially halted the repair scheme that was carried out as they concluded that the fix at the time was still unsafe.

Haier initially attempted to arrange a second repair for the machines that had already been seen to before the OPPS halted the operation.

The latest release will mean that the thousands of households with unsafe dryers will now be addressed.

News.title: Inside wild party holiday hotspot with cheap booze, wild sex games & naked bar dancing where rowdy Brits are welcome
News.content:
CLOTHES fly across the room as girls rush to rip off their bras and boys ditch their boxers.

Not a single person bats an eyelid when the underwear is thrown on to the bar and a winning team is announced.





It’s not because they are having sex — although that would probably be ignored too. It is simply part of a raunchy bar-crawl game.

Earlier in the evening, girls danced suggestively on the counter while lads came dressed in their best crop tops.

Welcome to Sunny Beach, Bulgaria — the only place you can cavort on a bar naked, according to the reps.

The Black Sea resort was recently declared the cheapest in Europe by the annual Post Office Travel Money Family Holiday report last year.

And the locals are grateful to the Balearic Islands for their attempts to throw out British revellers — as Bulgaria will have them and their money in a, ahem, flash.

‘Walk down street naked’

Matt Branch, 28, who has worked nine seasons in the party destination, knows first hand just how much Brits are loved in the resort.

The manager of events organiser Party Crew said: “They’re very welcome. I’m always told by locals that they want more Brits.

“There are no limits here. They just laugh at you if you act like an idiot.





“You could walk down the street naked after a certain time of night and people would just egg you on. Or they’d tell you to do another shot.

“It’s much freer than other party destinations. We tell people that it’s the only place you can get away with dancing naked on the bar.”

Lst year, in the Balearic and Canary Islands, as well as parts of mainland Spain, angry locals staged huge demonstrations against mass tourism, while the authorities in Magaluf, Ayia Napa and Ibiza tried to crack down on boisterous revellers.

In Barcelona, locals squirted foreigners with water pistols while they had lunch in protest at rising rents, which they blame on tourism.

Meanwhile, in Mallorca and Ibiza, mayors have banned the sale of booze from 9.30pm to 8am.

Yet Matt reckons other countries taking a tough line on tourists will simply make the Bulgarians even happier when the resort opens fully in June.

They will absolutely take advantage of other countries not wanting British tourists Matt Branch

He said: “When Spain limited the amount of free booze Bulgaria brought in premium all-inclusive deals, so Brits could get the same spirits as back home for free.

“They will absolutely take advantage of other countries not wanting British tourists.

“They’re passionate about their country, and as long as visitors from the UK love it, they love us.”

Matt and his team provide boat parties, bar crawls and even a Thailand-themed full moon party.



In the height of summer they have up to 200 people at one of their bar crawls, where punters play games including swapping clothes, taking off underwear and having shots poured straight into their mouths.

Bulgaria boasts a coastline of 234 miles, meaning surrendering just five miles — the length of Sunny Beach — to English, Irish, Welsh and Scottish tourists is worth it for locals.

The resort has been welcoming us since the 1990s, when the country established a buzzing nightlife, and now has more than 300,000 beds on offer in accommodation.

The owner of Mania Bar said: “British tourists are better than everybody. They are very good tourists who spend a lot of money. For them, it is very cheap here.

“We like to party as much as the English, so they are very welcome.”

Even workers who have put up with us for years are still happy for Brits to keep coming every summer.

Veteran resort worker Tsvetan Florov, the manager of Jack’s Bar, said: “British tourists will always be welcome in Sunny Beach.



“We like British people because they spend, although less this year than before, but I think that is due to the financial crisis back home.

‘Everyone is crazy here’

“Young tourists are crazy and badly behaved. It’s always crazy here. We just need to keep it all in one place, and then it is fine.”

Over his 20 years working in the resort’s bars and nightclubs, he has seen all possible bad behaviour.

He recalls: “I once saw a man getting a sexual favour at the bar, and he saw me and went ‘cheers’ with his drink.

“I looked down and saw the woman, and she raised her glass to me while she was doing it. A few years ago I saw girls dancing naked on the bar, which went down well with everyone.

“Later on it was lots of boys doing it ­— which was less welcome by everyone.”

Employees in bars and clubs say they trust that young people will keep coming and spending money.

One former Sunny Beach worker, who would only give his name as Chris, said: “We have to trust that the Brits will keep coming, which is why the resort expanded. British tourists spend much more than Eastern Europeans, especially on alcohol. We let them get away with more than other places would.”

One English reveller told me: “Everyone is crazy here. Anything goes — except weeing in the street.”

Bars have neon signs, boasting “save water, drink vodka” and “we want you to play beer pong”.



Pints are around £2, shots £1.50 and ten tequila slammers just £11.60 — but it’s not just booze on offer.

Dangerous hippy crack is being touted on the street, with eight people trying to flog the balloons in a 100-yard stretch.

In one club, five sellers of the gas are walking around the dance floor trying to tempt customers.

One balloon of the killer gas is just £3, but British tourists don’t seem to be interested in buying.

We heard it was a party place and it really is Sydney from Devon

Instead, they are focused on drinking as much as they can.

One Irish lad said: “It’s cheap as chips here. I love it.”

Devonshire girls Sydney, 19, and Bethany, 21, booked the resort after one of their dads recommended it.

Sydney said: “We heard it was a party place and it really is. It’s been amazing. We had two Sex On The Beaches earlier and Bethany already felt drunk, so we had to go get some water.”



A standard spirit measure in Bulgaria is between 50ml and 100ml, while in Britain it is 25ml — meaning there is more booze AND it is still cheaper than home.

‘Making the most of it’

Pals Ethan and Tom, both 25, from Wolverhampton, happily parade around the resort in lewd tops, one saying “I’ll eat your ass” and “Two seater” with arrows pointing up and down.

They were stopped by laughing locals who wanted a photo of them.

Ethan said: “Everyone here is making the most of it.

“Tom bought me this top and everyone seems to find it funny.”

One of the most popular beach bars is Viking, which has a show in the evening featuring dancing pirates who pour straight tequila into eager punters’ mouths.

They also offer a traffic light party, where revellers have a coloured neon band indicating if they are single, taken or simply hard to get.

In Beach Bar Mexo, punters are encouraged to dance on the bar, while in Central, on the main strip, trays of shots are frequently handed out, and they also pour booze directly into customers’ mouths.

Even the taxi drivers who work into the small hours don’t mind the boozing antics.

One said: “English tourists are good.”



When asked if we were badly behaved, he laughed and said: “It’s no problem.”

News.title: Abandoned UK theme park left overgrown & rotting for 14 years with graffiti-covered walls – as locals slam ‘chaos’ plans
News.content:
RIDE OFF Abandoned UK theme park left overgrown & rotting for 14 years with graffiti-covered walls – as locals slam ‘chaos’ plans

AN ABANDONED UK theme park has been decaying for 14 years – as locals slam new development plans as “absolute chaos”.

The Magical Kingdom of Camelot that once welcomed 500,000 visitors a year just outside of Chorley, Lancs, has become overgrown with graffiti-covered walls since closing its doors in 2012.





The medieval myth inspired park once featured thrilling rides and roller coasters such as the Whirlwind, Excalibur and the Knightmare – the most popular attraction rumoured to have cost £3mill to build.

Local legend has it that the area was once covered by the largest freshwater lake in England, Martin Mere, until it was drained in the 17th century.

Despite its 14-year closure, the park hosts an annual Scare City event for a live-action zombie experience every Halloween.

Facebook user Chris Willoughby took to the platform to share his pictures of the once beloved theme park and said: “Had a little walk down memory lane today round, what was, Camelot.

“Still can’t believe it closed. Had some great times with the family there! We use to go around 3-4 times a year over the summer months!”

Sparking the nostalgia of hundreds, commenters reminisced on the “great place”.

User Heather Whittle-Thompson said under the post: “Don’t think my heart could take going there looking around now the way it is.



“Such a shame nobody can make it what it was. It was always so busy we used to go most months when it was open, queuing to get in every time.”

Residents are fuming over proposals set to demolish the iconic Camelot theme park for 350 homes spanning over the 14 acre site.

Chorley councillor Alan Whittaker told the BBC: “350 houses means about 600 cars coming out on to Park Hall Road, which is not even a B-road.

“Everybody was concerned about the gridlock.

“But there are other issues like infrastructure, such as school availability, and GP surgeries.”



The developer, Story Homes, have previously applied for permission to build a similar site in both 2017 and 2019 but were rejected.

The fate of the controversial plans is in the hands of a government-appointed inspector and will be decided in the summer.

The Sun have reached out to Story Homes for comment.

News.title: 'Check now' as winner has just three weeks to claim £1million prize
News.content:
'Check now' as winner has just three weeks to claim £1million prize

If the money isn't claimed by May 3 it will be lost forever

View 3 Images Bundles of twenty pound sterling banknotes

A millionaire who has failed to claim their winning EuroMillions prize has just three weeks to contact lottery bosses or lose the money forever. Lottery bosses are trying to find the winner of a EuroMillions ticket purchased in the Unitary Authority of Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole worth £1,000,000.

‌



The search is on to find the owner of the winning ticket from the EuroMillions draw on November 4, 2025. The missing ticket has the winning Millionaire Maker code HPCF58869. The ticket-holder only has until midnight May 3, 2026 to claim their prize.

‌



Players are being urged to double-check their unique EuroMillions UK Millionaire Maker code for the chance to become an instant millionaire. For every EuroMillions line played, UK players automatically receive a EuroMillions Millionaire Maker code printed on their ticket.

‌



View 3 Images The money was won in a EuroMillions draw

Andy Carter, Senior Winners Advisor at Allwyn, operator of The National Lottery said, “It’s been around five months since the EuroMillions draw and we’ve not yet been contacted by the rightful ticket-holder. But where there is still time there’s hope. Think back to last winter, did you play the EuroMillions draw on Tuesday, November 4? Are there any warm coats that could be housing a lucky pink ticket?

‌



“Think back to that date and what you might have been doing at the time. Do you live in the area or were you passing through? Tell your friends and family, ask your colleagues – help us spread the word. It's our mission to unite the lucky winner with their prize.”

View 3 Images The money will go to good causes if not claimed

If no-one comes forward with the winning ticket before the prize claim deadline, then the prize money, plus all the interest it has generated, will go to help National Lottery-funded projects across the UK.

Article continues below

With all National Lottery draws, players have 180 days from the day of the draw to claim their prize if they have the winning ticket. Anyone who has any queries or who believes they have the winning ticket for any of the National Lottery draws within the 180-day deadline should call the National Lottery Line on 0333 234 5050 or email help@national-lottery.co.uk

News.title: Brit Virgin Atlantic cabin crew member arrested after 'pushing' teen at Disney park
News.content:
Brit Virgin Atlantic cabin crew member arrested after 'pushing' teen at Disney park

Keith Newman, 47, a crew member for Virgin Atlantic, is accused of pushing an 18-year-old at Disney’s Magic Kingdom, Florida, causing her to trip and spill water over a friend

View Image (Image: Orange County Jail)

A British air steward has been arrested after allegedly pushing a teenage girl who he claimed skipped a line at Disney’s Magic Kingdom.

Keith Newman, 47, a crew member for Virgin Atlantic, has been accused of pushing the 18-year-old at the Florida theme park, causing her to fall and spill water over a friend.

He claimed the girl jumped in front of him in the queue for Tiana’s Bayou Adventure ride – which is based on the Princess Tiana character from the Disney movie The Princess and the Frog. It is then understood that he put his arm out to stop her, saying “there’s a queue”.

The teenager said she tried to go around him, but “he pushed her back with both hands,” the Orange County Sheriff’s arrest report said.

She then is alleged to have fallen backwards into her friend and got wet because she spilled her water bottle over herself, the arrest report said. But otherwise, the victim wasn’t hurt, the arrest report said and did not ask for medical treatment.

Article continues below

Newman denied pushing her but the victim’s friend corroborated the story when interviewed by police. It is reported that the friend said she heard Newman say: "There is a queue,” before going to push the teenager back with an arm.

And then it is alleged by the friend that the victim “was not letting Keith push her back,” so Newman used both hands to shove her back. But Newman claims he simply put his hand out and the victim walked into it, the arrest report said.

News.title: Keir Starmer hits back at Donald Trump's attack on UK - 'I'm not going to yield'
News.content:
Keir Starmer hits back at Donald Trump's attack on UK - 'I'm not going to yield'

During PMQs, Keir Starmer warned he will 'not yield' as he suggested Donald Trump had been trying to pressure him over the UK's stance on the conflict in the Middle East

View 2 Images The PM was asked about the US President's latest threat to Britain over a trade deal (Image: PA)

Keir Starmer has warned he will not change his mind on the Iran war after Donald Trump lashed out at the UK again.

‌



The PM, who was asked about the US President's latest threat to Britain over a trade deal, warned he will "not yield" as he suggested Mr Trump had been trying to pressure him over the UK's stance on the conflict.

‌



Mr Trump has repeatedly criticised the UK after Mr Starmer refused to jump into supporting US/Israeli military action in the Middle East. Overnight, the US President hit out at the "sad" state of the US-UK special relationship

‌



During PMQs, Lib Dem leader Sir Ed Davey asked the PM about Mr Trump's threat "to rip up his trade deal with the UK as punishment for us not joining his idiotic war in Iran".

He told Mr Starmer that this must be the "last straw" and that No10 should cancel King Charles's state visit to the US next month. "Mr Trump is the most unpredictable President in history and I hope he will not embarrass the monarch.," he added.

Donald Trump threatens UK and lashes out at 'sad' state of special relationship READ MORE :

View 2 Images Donald Trump lashed out at the "sad" state of the US-UK special relationship (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Mr Starmer replied: "My position on the Iran war has been clear from the start. We're not going to get dragged into this war. It is not our war. A lot of pressure has been applied to me to take a different course and that pressure included what happened last night.

"I'm not going to change my mind. I'm not going to yield. It is not in our national interest to join this war. We will not do so. I know where I stand.

"In relation to the King's visit, the purpose of the visit is to mark the 250th anniversary of relations and independence, obviously, of the US. The monarchy is an important reminder of the long standing bonds and enduring relationship between our two countries, which a far greater than anyone who occupies any particular office at any particular time."

‌



In an interview with Sky News overnight, Mr Trump said he liked Mr Starmer, but hit out at the UK government's policies on energy and immigration. According to the broadcaster, Mr Trump first reportedly replied "with whom" when asked how he would describe the special relationship right now.

He then said: "How is the relationship? It's the relationship where: when we asked them for help, they were not there. When we needed them, they were not there. When we didn't need them, they were not there. And they still aren't there."

The US President then warned: "Well it's been better, but it's sad. And we gave them a good trade deal, better than I had to, which can always be changed." He also said of the PM: "I like Starmer - but I think he's made a tragic mistake in closing North Sea oil. You see your energy prices are the highest in the world."

Article continues below

Pressed whether the strained relationship will overshadow the King's Royal visit to the United States later this month, he replied: "No. Not at all. I've known the King for a long time and he is not involved in that process."

News.title: Iranian troops gear up for a return to war as Straits crisis deepens
News.content:
Iranian troops gear up for a return to war as Straits crisis deepens

Chilling signs all-out war could return to the Gulf region as Iranian troops have been spotted digging out hidden rocket and missile launchers from underground chambers in case talks fail

View 5 Images Hormuz blockade: US Presidend Donald Trump (Image: Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Iranian forces are using the temporary halt in fighting to re-arm with hidden missile launchers buried by US - Israeli air-strikes. They have been detected digging out the firing mechanisms from underground storage depots as the Strait of Hormuz crisis deepens. Satellite footage has been analysed showing mechanical diggers working on freeing up deadly launchers from previously attacked sites.

‌



It comes after the US imposed a naval blockade on the maritime chokepoint in a bid to punish Iran for first blocking the waterway. Sources suggest Iran is using a temporary truce signed on April 8, which expires on the 22nd, to move missile assets from east to west. One of the buried sites is at Khomein, birthplace of the founder of the Islamic Republic Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomenei. His successor Ayatollah Khamenei was killed in the opening days of the war in an Israeli air-strike on his Tehran compound.

‌



View 5 Images The Strait of Hormuz crisis has deepened (Image: @IraninHyderabad/X)

‌



China defies Trump and sails tanker through Strait of Hormuz blockade in show of force READ MORE :

It is also believed the US re-configuring and arming up its armada based in the Gulf region both to impose the blockade and re-start the conflict if needed. The US military has insisted it has “completely halted economic trade going into and out of Iran by sea, as its blockade enters a second day.

Lebanon and Israel have had their first talks in three decades amid a growing humanitarian crisis because of the Hezbollah-Israel missile war. Only this morning on Wednesday there were reports Lebanese Hezbollah had opened fire on northern Israel with missiles and rockets in a huge attack.

View 5 Images Musician plays in Iran's Minab scene of terrible strike (Image: Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

‌



The Lebanon - Israel talks in Washington are the first they have held since 1993.

Over 2,000 people have been killed since Israeli military operations in Lebanon began again on 2 March, just days after US and Israeli strikes started in Iran.

While the two sides were meeting in Washington on Tuesday, Hezbollah claimed at least 24 attacks on Israel and Israeli troops in Lebanon. Drone and rocket alarms sounded in communities across northern Israel for much of the day. Israeli missions in Lebanon are aimed at disarming and dismantling Hezbollah, which it has fought since the October 7 Gaza war started.

‌



View 5 Images Tyre, Lebanon, after Israeli air-strike (Image: Getty Images)

US CENTCOM, which oversees security and crisis management of 20 nations in the Middle East and Central/ South Asia says thousands of troops are involved. CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper said in a statement: “An estimated 90% of Iran’s economy is fuelled by international trade by sea.

“In less than 36 hours since the blockade was implemented, US forces have completely halted economic trade going into and out of Iran by sea.” CENTCOM said that more than 10,000 sailors, Marines and US Air Force personnel are taking part in the operation.

Article continues below

View 5 Images Southern Tehran after strikes (Image: Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

It said that, in the first 24 hours, six merchant ships had complied with US orders and been forced to turn around and re-enter an Iranian port. It is believed a US Navy destroyer intercepted two oil tankers attempting to leave Iran on Tuesday, a day after the blockade went into effect, and instructed them to turn around.

News.title: 110 women were killed by men in one year - but justice caught up with this thug
News.content:
110 women were killed by men in one year - but justice caught up with this thug

Cowardly Simon Ghebremedhin, 34, stabbed 26-year-old Marjama Osman in her own home before knifing himself and trying to cover up the crime by accusing his victim of attacking him

View 3 Images Marjama Osman was murdered in her own home (Image: Met Police)

A thug who murdered one of 110 women killed by men in the UK in just one year has been jailed for life.

‌



Simon Ghebremedhin, 34, stabbed 26-year-old Marjama Osman in her own home before plunging the blade into himself and claiming his victim was the aggressor.

‌



Marjama, who knew Ghebremedhin, managed to escape her flat in Croydon, south London, on May 31, last year before collapsing outside, where she was found unconscious by a passer-by. She was one of 110 women murdered by men whose names were read out to Parliament last month by Home Office minister Jess Phillips on International Women's Day.

‌



View 3 Images Simon Ghebremedhin was jailed for life (Image: Met Police)

Police chiefs announce mandatory recording of officer suicides after sergeant takes own life READ MORE :

MPs fell silent as Ms Phillips carried out the sombre tradition for the 11th year of honouring women killed by a man or where a man had been charged in the previous year.

A jury at Inner London Crown Court found Ghebremedhin guilty of murder earlier this month and he was sentenced on Tuesday to life imprisonment with a minimum term of 19 years. Police and paramedics attended, but they were unable to save Marjama.

‌



Ghebremedhin was also found at the scene with a stab wound to his abdomen and was taken to hospital. He later claimed he had acted in self-defence, telling officers Marjama had attacked him with a knife.

View 3 Images Home Office minister Jess Phillips has called for justice for women (Image: Nicola tree)

However, CCTV footage showed him acting aggressively before the attack, including smashing his own phone and banging on Marjama's door. After chasing Marjama out of her flat, he returned inside, where police believe he injured himself in an attempt to support his false account.

‌



Specialists later concluded the wound was likely self-inflicted. Det Insp Aytac Necati, who led the investigation, said: “Our thoughts today are with Marjama’s family and friends. The evidence presented at trial was graphic and highly distressing, which meant Marjama’s loved ones were subjected to further torment and anguish.

“Ghebremedhin is a particularly devious killer, who went to great lengths to deceive police and the court. Thankfully, diligent detective work has exposed him as a liar.

“The Met is committed to protecting the public from harm – with violence against women and girls a particular focus of our New Met for London strategy. The successful prosecution in this case illustrates this commitment. We’ll continue to do everything in our power to take the most dangerous and prolific perpetrators off our streets.”

Article continues below

Ms Phillips read the list collated by Counting Dead Women - the Femicide Census' sister project. The Home Office minister first read out the names of women killed by men in 2016.

She told MPs: "The reason I stood to be elected to Parliament in the first place is that while we are gathered here in the heart of our democracy to discuss these issues in comfort and in safety, beyond these walls, in every part of our country, women and girls are suffering. They are being attacked, abused, harassed and stalked at home, in public places and online. The scale of violence against women and girls shames our society.”

After reading the list of names, she called for the women to "get the justice that they deserved" and for them to be honoured "by preventing others from suffering the same fate".

News.title: Eight-week-old baby hospitalised with meningitis B despite not showing key symptom
News.content:
Eight-week-old baby hospitalised with meningitis B despite not showing key symptom

Mum Elise told how her baby daughter Coralie 'looked up at her terrified' as she was rushed to hospital at just eight weeks old after contracting the deadly meningitis B strain

View 5 Images Baby Coralie developed the deadly Meningitis B variant (Image: Elise Wedderburn / SWNS)

An eight-week-old baby was rushed to hospital after developing a deadly meningitis variant - despite having no rash.

‌



Little Coralie Wedderburn had just been for her eight-week check up when she suddenly fell ill, and was taken to The Queen Mother Hospital in Margate. Mum Elise and dad Stewart feared the worst as she slipped in and out of consciousness, with tests showing she had contracted the more severe bacterial meningitis B strain.

‌



This is the same type which caused the outbreak in Canterbury last month, leaving two dead. Now, 11-week-old Coralie, who was "fit and well" before the illness, is recovering at home.

‌



View 5 Images The emergency hospital admission came despite eight-week-old Coralie showing no symptoms (Image: Elise Wedderburn / SWNS)

I thought I had a headache - what followed was the worst experience of my life READ MORE :

NHS worker Elise, 40, wondered whether her daughter's illness was linked to last month's Canterbury outbreak - but there is understood to have been no connection. Mum-of-six Elise from Herne Bay, Kent, said: "It’s been like a nightmare.

"I don’t think it’s really sunk in. She had no symptoms at all. No rash, no temperature. It’s scary to think what would have happened if we hadn’t taken her to get checked."

‌



Coralie and her twin brother William were vaccinated against meningitis and other ailments when they had their eight-week check up on March 26. Elise noticed she was "under the weather" that night and the day after, but assumed it was a cold or flu, and gave her Calpol.

View 5 Images She had just been for her eight-week check up when she fell ill (Image: Elise Wedderburn / SWNS)

Alarm bells only started to ring when Elise got up to feed the twins during the night and Coralie only drank half her bottle of milk. The next day, she was the same but just had a strange look in her eyes," Elise added.

‌



"She looked really scared. She was very pale and sleepy. She was looking up at me terrified and something told me she wanted someone to help her," she said. Symptoms for meningococcal disease, which can cause meningitis, include rashes, fever, vomiting and severe headaches.

Coralie's temperature was fine and she had "no symptoms" but Elise had a "gut feeling" that "something wasn't right". She said: "I had no idea what it was but because she had had the vaccinations two days before, I was keeping a close eye on her."

Financial adviser Stewart, 45, took Coralie to a walk-in Urgent Treatment Centre at Queen Victoria Memorial Hospital the same day. And after a heel prick test showed a dangerously low blood pressure level, medics there called an ambulance to take her to QEQM in Canterbury.

‌



View 5 Images Mum Elise said she 'feared the worst' when her baby was taken into resus (Image: Elise Wedderburn / SWNS)

After arriving at A&E, she spent three hours in a resuscitation bay receiving fluids and IV antibiotics, losing consciousness repeatedly. "You’re just taking each second at a time," Elise said.

"Initially in the resus, I feared the worst. You could see the panic from the doctors and nurses and obviously, working in a hospital myself, I know the signs. You just want to take it all away from her. She was surrounded by people at the bed. She looked like a completely different baby."

‌



Coralie underwent a CT scan and an X-Ray while medics put her on three separate antibiotics and one antiviral anti-medication while they searched for the cause of her illness. "We thought meningitis was the last thing it could be," Elise said.

On March 30, after a spinal tap, doctors confirmed Coralie had bacterial meningitis B. Elise said: "When they told us it was meningitis, I was actually driving and my husband told me to pull over and he told me. We were really shocked."

But the same day, antibiotics Coralie started to show signs of improvement. Elise added: "She started to look brighter. Every hour I felt like I was seeing more light in her face. From the Wednesday, they said 'we’re going to try feeding her' and she managed to take a little bit of milk from the bottle."

‌



View 5 Images She is now recovering at home (Image: Elise Wedderburn / SWNS)

Coralie has since had an ultrasound scan on her head and is awaiting an MRI to "get a clearer picture" of the long-term effects. She was discharged on Good Friday and is now recovering - but Elise has no idea how she picked up the infection.

Elise said: "The week before, we didn’t really go anywhere. I’d taken them out for walks in the pram but the only people who had contact with her with family."

Article continues below

It is understood Whole Genome Sequencing tests found no link between Coralie's illness and the outbreak which saw two young people lose their lives last month. A University of Kent student aged 21 and Juliette Kenny, an 18-year-old sixth former at a school in Faversham, died from meningitis after multiple people were infected in the Canterbury area.

The outbreak reportedly started at the Club Chemistry nightclub, with the first case identified on March 13. Tens of thousands of antibiotics and vaccines were offered to people in the area, but the outbreak appeared to have been halted after UK Health Security Agency announced on March 26 that there had been no new cases.

News.title: Moment laughing killer fist bumps friend after knifing student to death
News.content:
Moment laughing killer fist bumps friend after knifing student to death

Dino Donaldson is facing a life sentence for the murder of Anojan Gnaneswaran after bragging: 'I stabbed him through the back bro, I stabbed him fully. I watched it and I felt it go in him, yeah'

British Transport Police share footage of Dino Donaldson's arrest

This is the moment a drug dealer laughs on a night bus after murdering a university student and boasting "I stabbed him fully".

‌



Dino Donaldson, 21, was caught on CCTV smiling and joking after repeatedly plunging a blade into Anojan Gnaneswaran, 21, at Strawberry Hill train station in Twickenham, south west London. Donaldson was also captured on the audio of a doorbell camera bragging: "I stabbed him through the back bro, I stabbed him fully. I watched it and I felt it go in him, yeah."

‌



He knifed his terrified victim in the chest, abdomen and thigh after chasing him onto train tracks on January 8, 2024. A fight had broken out on the station platform between two groups of men over a drug deal to pay £50 for 10 ecstasy tablets.

‌



View 2 Images Laughing Donaldson fist bumps a friend (Image: PA)

Police chiefs announce mandatory recording of officer suicides after sergeant takes own life READ MORE :

Anojan, a third year accounting and finance student who competed in the World and European championships in karate, was pronounced dead at the scene. Less than an hour later, Donaldson was caught on CCTV on an N87 night bus smiling and laughing.

Wearing a black hooded top and puffer jacket while sitting on the back seat of the top deck, he leans over grinning and fist bumps a friend while they appear to share a joke. Donaldson was arrested at his home in west London three days later where he was discovered hiding in a cupboard.

‌



View 2 Images Police body worn footage of Donaldson being arrested (Image: PA)

Police found 74 wraps of crack and heroin in his bedroom with a street value of more than £1,000. Following the unanimous verdict at the Old Bailey on Tuesday, Judge Angela Rafferty KC remanded the defendant in custody and adjourned sentencing to a date to be fixed.

British Transport Police Det Chief Insp Paul Attwell said: “What started as an argument over a drug deal ended in a young man’s life being cut short by a remorseless thug. Donaldson showed his true colours as a coward by arming himself with a knife that night.

‌



“His cowardice has continued by never accepting responsibility and admitting his crime – thankfully the jury saw through his lies. While no verdict can ever compensate for the loss of Anojan, I hope today’s outcome provides his family with some sense of closure.

“Thanks to our extensive investigation, justice has now been served to the man responsible for killing their loved one.”

Anojan’s family paid tribute to a “much-loved son and brother”. In a statement issued through police, they said: “Anojan was in his third year at university studying accounting and finance, and he was so excited for his future.

Article continues below

“He excelled at all sports and had achieved first-dan black belt in karate – he competed in the World and European championships in karate, and we will all miss him so much.”

Rory McIlroy has the skill and mental fortitude to potentially secure up to 10 Masters titles, according to former Open champion Padraig Harrington.

The bold prediction follows McIlroy’s recent triumph at Augusta National, where the 36-year-old joined an elite group of Jack Nicklaus, Sir Nick Faldo and Tiger Woods in successfully defending his title.

Harrington, a back-to-back Open winner from 2007 and the 2008 PGA Championship victor, believes McIlroy’s performance underscores his capacity for sustained dominance at the iconic course. The 54-year-old Irishman, whose best finishes at Augusta were two ties for fifth, sees no obstacle to McIlroy cementing his legacy as a multiple Masters champion.

"As regards to Masters, Rory could win 10 of them at this stage, or five of them anyway," Harrington stated at a press conference ahead of the Senior PGA Championship in Bradenton, Florida.

He added, "he probably will still be competitive at 50 years of age around that golf course."

Harrington highlighted McIlroy’s evolving game as a key factor.

open image in gallery McIlroy defended his Masters title on Sunday ( PA )

"For him, it was interesting that he won that one with his short game, which makes him even better a player," he observed. "Over the years it is physicality to driving and the iron play. He has always been a superb chipper, but now it is with the putting and things like that.

“A very rounded game and a game that looks like it has a lot of longevity in it, so he is in a very nice place going forward, particularly at that tournament."

The Irishman further emphasised the significance of McIlroy’s second Masters victory.

"It is amazing when you win one, that he has now got two and we are thinking that maybe two or three or five would be realistic around that golf course."

McIlroy’s victory was also a testament to his mental resilience. He recovered from seeing a six-shot second-round lead evaporate on Saturday, only to regain control with successive birdies through Amen Corner.

open image in gallery Padraig Harrington thinks McIlroy could win 10 Masters titles ( PA )

Harrington, who shares a sports psychologist, Dr Bob Rotella, with McIlroy, was particularly impressed by the Northern Irishman’s composure in securing the green jacket, finishing a stroke ahead of world number one Scottie Scheffler.

"He showed some real good character there, psychology-wise he really won that tournament," Harrington remarked. "His mentality and how he went about things, that is a very strong showing for him.

“He obviously still has the physical side of the game, but to show that short game and the mental side of the game means he looks like he would be a very strong force for a while to come in the game."

Two major driving schools owned by the AA have been ordered to refund more than 80,000 customers and pay a £4.2m fine by the UK’s competition watchdog for engaging in an illegal pricing tactic.

The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) found that AA Driving School and BSM Driving School omitted a mandatory £3 booking fee from their advertised upfront prices.

This practice, known as drip-pricing, meant that learner drivers were not shown the full cost of their lessons initially, with the fee only appearing later in the booking process.

Individual refunds will vary depending on the number of lesson packages purchased, averaging around £9 per customer, and totalling more than £760,000. The combined refunds and penalty will amount to nearly £5m. This marks the first financial penalty issued by the CMA for a breach of consumer law since it gained new enforcement powers.

Sarah Cardell, the CMA chief executive, said: “If a fee is mandatory, the law is clear: it must be included in the price from the very start – not added at checkout – so consumers always know what they need to pay.

“At a time when people are watching every pound, dripped fees can tip the balance. And when it comes to something as important – and costly – as learning to drive, people deserve clarity.

Two major driving schools owned by the AA have been ordered to refund more than 80,000 customers ( PA Archive )

“With our new powers, it will never pay to break the law or treat consumers unfairly. Where the rules are ignored, we’ll step in to put things right.”

A spokesperson for AA driving schools said: “Although the £3 booking fee was made clear to customers before their purchase, we acknowledge it should have also been displayed at the start of the online booking journey.

“Having listened to the regulator, we made immediate changes to our website to make the £3 booking fee more prominent.

“We are now refunding all relevant customers. Whilst we are disappointed with the outcome of the investigation, we have fully cooperated with the CMA throughout and would emphasise that protecting consumer rights has been central to our business for more than 120 years.”

The decision comes after the Department for Business and Trade reported in 2023 that nearly half of online businesses used dripped fees, costing consumers up to £3.5bn annually.

Who is eligible for a refund?

The CMA launched its investigation in November 2025 and found that people booking lessons between April and December that year were initially shown prices that did not include the mandatory booking fee.

New customers were instead only shown this at the booking stage, after they had already selected lessons, chosen times, and entered personal details.

This practice is known as “drip-pricing”, which is illegal and can mislead customers into believing the product or service they were buying was a lower price than they would later be charged.

The average payout will be around £9, the CMA has said, adding that affected customers do not need to take any action. AA Driving School or BSM Driving School will contact them directly, confirming that the money will be automatically refunded to the card used for payment. If this is not possible, a cheque will be issued.

It's officially Tax Day in the U.S. And if you’ve waited till the last minute to file your 2025 return, don’t panic. You still have time to get it done.

If you're worried that you still might not be able to finish your taxes in time, you also can file for an extension, which will give you until Oct. 15 to file.

Here's what you need to know about Wednesday's deadline — and a few tips to keep in mind.

What do I need to file my tax return?

Generally, every tax-filer needs the following at hand

— your Social Security number

— W-2 forms, if you're employed

— 1099-G forms, if you're unemployed

— 1099 forms, if you're self-employed

— Savings and investment records

— A sense of any eligible deductions, such as education expenses, medical bills or charitable donations.

— A sense of relevant tax credits, such as the child tax credit or a retirement savings contributions credit.

To find a more detailed document list, visit the IRS website.

Tax professionals recommend gathering all your documents in one place before you start your tax return — as well as having documents from the year prior, if your financial situation has changed drastically. Experts also suggest creating an identity protection PIN number with the IRS to guard against identity theft. Once you create a number, the IRS will require it to file your tax return.

How do I file for an extension?

If you run out of time to file your tax return, you can file for an extension to take more time by using your preferred tax software, with the IRS Free File tool, or via mail.

However, it’s important to remember that the extension is only to file your tax return, not to pay owed taxes. If you owe taxes, you should pay an estimated amount before the deadline to avoid paying penalties and interest. If you expect to receive a refund, you’ll still receive your money when you file your taxes.

The deadline to file for an extension is Wednesday, which will give you until Oct. 15 to file.

The IRS notes some taxpayers — including members of the military and people who live and work outside of the U.S. — get an automatic, two-month extension to file until June 15. But again, most payments are still due April 15.

How can I avoid mistakes filing my taxes?

Many people fear getting in trouble with the IRS if they make a mistake. To avoid common errors:

— Double check your name on your Social Security card.

You'll want to make sure the name on your tax return matches what's on your Social Security card. Some people may have taken a new last name after marriage, for example, but if that hasn't been updated with the Social Security Administration yet, the IRS notes you'll need to use your former name to avoid delays.

And if you get a W-2 from an employer with a name that no longer matches your Social Security card, the IRS says you should contact your employer to fix it.

— Search for tax statements if you've opted out of paper mail.

While many important tax documents are still sent out on physical paper, people increasingly are opting out of snail mail these days. If you're not seeing it in your mailbox, check your online accounts.

“If you didn’t get anything in the mail doesn’t mean that there isn’t an information document out there that you need to be aware of and report accordingly,” Tom O’Saben, director of tax content and government relations at the National Association of Tax Professionals, previously told The Associated Press.

— Report all of your income.

If you had more than one job in 2025, you need the W-2 forms for each.

What resources are available?

For those who made $89,000 or less last year, IRS Free File offers free guided tax preparation that does the math for you. And if you have questions while working on your tax forms, the IRS also offers an interactive tax assistant tool.

Beyond TurboTax and H&R Block, taxpayers can also hire licensed professionals, such as certified public accountants. The IRS offers a directory of tax preparers across the United States.

The IRS also funds two types of programs that offer free tax help: Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) and the Tax Counseling for the Elderly program (TCE). People who earn $69,000 or less a year, those who have a disability, and those who speak limited English all qualify for the VITA program. Those who are 60 or older qualify for the TCE program. The IRS has a site for locating organizations that host VITA and TCE clinics.

If you have a tax problem, there are also clinics around the country that can help you resolve these issues. Generally, these tax clinics also offer services in other languages such as Spanish, Chinese and Vietnamese.

____

AP Business Writer Wyatte Grantham-Philips contributed to this report.

Arvid Lindblad has described F1 as one of the “biggest five sports in the world” as he lifted the lid on his first month as a driver on the grid.

The 18-year-old Briton has impressed in the first three races of his rookie season, scoring points on his debut with an eighth-place finish at the season-opener in Australia.

Lindblad also qualified in the top-10 at the Japanese Grand Prix, with teammate Liam Lawson finishing in the points in Suzuka. Racing Bulls are just two points behind the group’s senior team in Red Bull in the constructors’ championship.

F1’s popularity has boomed in recent years, with more races than ever before and more record-breaking grand prix attendance records. Asked by The Independent what the biggest surprise has been, Lindblad admitted the scale of the sport stood out, as well as duties away from the racetrack.

“It’s probably just the amount of our job that isn’t driving, especially compared to other categories,” he said on Tuesday. “That’s the way the sport is going and that’s the way a lot of sports are going.

“There’s also an appreciation of how big the sport is. I’ve been in the F1 paddock on F2 and F3 weekends, but it’s just appreciating how many fans are there.

“How big is the sport? I would say one of the top five sports in the world. So that’s pretty cool to be a part of.”

Lindblad, as opposed to many drivers on the grid, also moved to downplay criticisms of the new regulations.

“I haven’t found the cars that bad at the moment,” he added. “There are some things on the PU [power unit] side which are not the easiest.

“On one side, I do quite enjoy the challenge of having something new and different to deal with. It’s another element where you can make a difference. I also think the cars are actually quite nice to drive.

“They’re more nimble. There’s less errors, it’s easier to follow. They’re not stiff. There are pros and cons to it.”

F1 next goes racing at the Miami Grand Prix on 1-3 May.

Pizza chain Franco Manca is poised to close around 16 of its restaurants, a restructuring move anticipated to affect around 225 jobs.

The decision by parent group The Fulham Shore, which also operates The Real Greek chain, has been attributed partly to "disproportionately high" UK taxes and a lack of business rates relief for restaurants.

The company stated that a "minority of its sites" were "no longer sustainable".

While the specific locations among Franco Manca’s roughly 70 outlets have not yet been disclosed, Fulham Shore boss Marcel Khan confirmed that a Company Voluntary Arrangement (CVA) restructuring process will be launched for the pizza business.

It comes two months after bosses hired advisers to look at strategic options including a potential sale or a restructure.

It is understood that Fulham Shore is continuing to review future options for the 28-strong Real Greek chain.

open image in gallery Franco Manca is set to shut around 16 restaurants as part of a CVA restructuring (Fulham Shore/PA) ( Fulham Shore )

Fulham Shore was bought by Japanese restaurant group Toridoll, with backing from investment firm Capdesia, in 2023 for £93.4 million.

Mr Khan, chief executive of Fulham Shore, said: “Even restaurant businesses that are doing all the right things from a customer and operational perspective are not immune to widely publicised pressures impacting the hospitality industry.

“This includes significant increases in national insurance and the national living wage in recent history, as well as a lack of business rates relief for the restaurant sector and disproportionately high VAT in the UK compared with Europe.”

He added: “As a result of these external cost pressures, we have to make sure that we are putting our business on a sustainable footing for long-term growth and development.

“This is why we have taken the difficult decision to undertake a CVA for Franco Manca, which will see a minority proportion of our restaurants closing where they are no longer sustainable in this cost environment.

“We are deeply saddened by the closures of a minority proportion of our restaurants, and will support our affected team members throughout this process in every way that we can.”

Rachel Reeves is said to be digging her heels in over a major increase to defence spending, despite warnings that Britain is “in peril” as a result of its ailing military.

The armed forces are thought to be facing a financial black hole of around £28bn over the next four years, but the chancellor has reportedly only approved plans for a “limited” increase to the Ministry of Defence’s budget amid concerns over how the Iran war will affect the public finances.

Sky News reported that defence chiefs will meet this week to discuss what is expected to be a £3.5bn cut to the military budget for the current financial year.

And UK military chiefs have been asked to find billions in “efficiencies”, despite Sir Keir Starmer saying he is readying his armed forces for war, the broadcaster reported.

open image in gallery Families are bearing the cost of the conflict, says the chancellor ( PA )

The chancellor’s proposal for an increase to the defence budget of just £10bn, reported by The Times, comes as she draws up plans for a targeted energy bailout for vulnerable households.

Rachel Reeves is also expected to slash plans to hike fuel duty in September, a policy that is expected to cost around £2.6bn.

Sources told the newspaper that Ms Reeves is not willing to break her fiscal rules or increase taxes to ramp up defence spending.

This is despite several stark warnings from key military figures in the face of growing global turbulence, with escalating conflict in the Middle East and the ongoing war in Ukraine.

On Tuesday, a number of former defence secretaries and Labour grandees rowed in behind a former Nato secretary general, who warned that the UK’s security is “in peril” as a result of the “corrosive complacency” of Sir Keir Starmer.

George Robertson, a former Labour defence secretary who was appointed by the prime minister to write the government’s Strategic Defence Review (SDR), used a speech on Tuesday to accuse “non-military experts” in the Treasury of “vandalism” and to claim Sir Keir is unwilling “to make the necessary investment” in Britain’s defence.

Piling in on Lord Robertson’s criticisms, Sir Malcolm Rifkind, a former defence secretary, argued that the government’s “prime responsibility” is defence, and called for ministers to fund this through a cut to welfare or an increase in income tax.

Jack Straw, who was foreign secretary under Tony Blair, praised Lord Robertson’s intervention, telling The Independent: “As George points out, there is a great urgency to settle the defence spending programme at a level which meets our needs, now and in the future, and with that make necessary decisions to cut non-essential welfare spending.”

Meanwhile, former Tory defence secretary Ben Wallace said: “Lord Robertson, like the rest of us, has become increasingly frustrated with a prime minister who talks the talk but doesn’t follow it up with funding and action. The PM needs to show leadership, not spin, on our defence.”

And on Wednesday, Fiona Hill, a former White House chief adviser and another co-author of Britain’s SDR, also joined Lord Robertson’s criticisms, warning of a “bizarre” lack of urgency in defence planning.

She told The Guardian: “What George is saying, very bluntly, is there is basically a lack of resolute leadership on this. Because everybody’s worried about votes and, you know, reactions, and all of this on the left and on the right.”

Downing Street hit back at Lord Robertson’s assertion that Britain was “underprepared” and “underinsured”, with the prime minister’s official spokesperson saying: “I completely reject that. Our armed forces, as I say, are working around the world every minute of the day to keep us safe at home.”

The government has promised to publish a 10-year defence investment plan to fund the SDR, but it has been beset by repeated delays – something that has sparked criticism and concern from MPs on both sides of the Commons.

open image in gallery Lord George Robertson issued a stark warning over the state of Britain’s defence ( Getty )

Meanwhile, in-year savings were blamed for a delay in sending HMS Dragon to Cyprus weeks after the Iran crisis began and the UK’s base on the island came under attack from Tehran.

There are also ongoing questions about the reduction of the size of the army, which is down to around 70,000 personnel and using poor and outdated heavy vehicles and tanks.

Sir Keir told MPs on Monday that the government was working to finalise the defence investment plan, but he did not want to repeat the mistakes of previous administrations because “we inherited plans that were unfunded and not deliverable”.

The government has committed to spending 2.5 per cent of gross domestic product on defence by 2027, increasing to 3 per cent in the next parliament and a Nato-agreed target of 3.5 per cent by 2035.

Ms Reeves is set to meet her US counterpart Scott Bessent in Washington on Wednesday after he argued “a small bit of economic pain” caused by the Iran war was worth it to prevent Tehran from getting a nuclear weapon.

The comments by the US treasury secretary put him at odds with the chancellor, who has gone public with her anger and frustration at the “folly” of America’s actions in the Middle East and its financial fallout on families.

The pair were due to hold face-to-face talks during the spring meetings of the International Monetary Fund, which will be dominated by the ongoing crisis in the Gulf. The war has inflicted a global economic shock and sent energy prices soaring.

A government spokesperson said: “We have delivered the largest sustained increase in defence spending since the Cold War – taking the total investment to more than £270bn across this parliament.

“We are finalising our Defence Investment Plan that we will publish as soon as possible, rebuilding British industry to make defence an engine for growth and doubling down on our own commitment to Nato.”

News.title: Trump’s blockade appears to be turning back tankers in the Strait of Hormuz – but Iran has a trick up its sleeve
News.content:
